statement: Restaurants that score 14 or more points (not A-range) at a routine initial inspection draw more 311 Food Poisoning complaints in the following 365 days than restaurants that score 0-13, after borough, cuisine, chain status and quarter, and the excess is larger than for Noise - Commercial complaints at the same lots.

graph_evidence.association_id: RzNvMLQc9u (variable) protection from contamination violation -> outbreak level
graph_evidence.summary: Minnesota chain outbreak (Firestone 2020): a protection-from-contamination violation at the last routine inspection, OR 4.92 (1.57-15.39) for outbreak level; 54 restaurants.

graph_evidence.association_id: FCDuRbXqiy (variable) evidence of vermin -> food-borne outbreaks
graph_evidence.summary: Miami-Dade 1995 case-control (Cruz 2001): overall inspection outcome and number of critical violations did not differ between outbreak and control restaurants; only vermin, OR 3.3 (1.1-13.1).
US local health departments (Li 2011): complaint and outbreak rates correlate, r = 0.38; complaints detect a median 69% of outbreaks.

graph_evidence.association_id: CCatfE2F4k (variable) chain restaurants -- violations per inspection
graph_evidence.summary: Philadelphia 2013-2014 (Leinwand 2017): chains 6.5 against 9.6 violations per inspection; used here as a covariate.

literature.citation: Irwin K et al. Am J Public Health 1989;79:586-590 (PMID 2705592)
literature.finding: Seattle-King County, 28 outbreak restaurants and 56 matched controls: poor routine scores 5 times, temperature-control violations 10 times more likely in outbreak restaurants.

literature.citation: Jones TF et al. Emerg Infect Dis 2004;10:688-692 (PMID 15200861)
literature.finding: Tennessee 1993-2000, 167,574 inspections: mean scores of outbreak restaurants did not differ from others; inspector means ranged 69-92.

literature.citation: Petran RL, White BW, Hedberg CW. J Food Prot 2012;75:2016-2027 (PMID 23127711)
literature.finding: No overall association between routine inspection scores and outbreak inspection scores at outbreak restaurants; some specific violations more likely.
NYC Yelp pilot: of 468 illness reviews only 3% had been reported to DOHMH by phone or online, so 311 complaints are a small, selected share of illness.

literature.citation: Wong MR et al. Am J Public Health 2015;105:e81-e87 (PMID 25602861)
literature.finding: NYC letter grading: probability of an A-range score on unannounced inspection +35% (31-40%) three years after launch.

literature.citation: Firestone MJ, Hedberg CW. Emerg Infect Dis 2018;24:2164-2168 (PMID 30457518)
literature.finding: Salmonella rates in NYC fell 5.3% a year relative to the rest of New York State after letter grading (2011-2015 against 2006-2010).

literature.citation: Jin GZ, Leslie P. Q J Econ 2003;118:409-451
literature.finding: Los Angeles grade cards raised hygiene scores and were followed by a fall in foodborne-illness hospitalisations (about 20%). Not in PubMed; abstract not read here, cited from the paper's published summary.

prediction.magnitude: IRR (not-A against A-range) 1.10 to 1.60, midpoint 1.33. The literature is split: Irwin 1989 found poor scores predict outbreaks (about 5 times), Cruz 2001, Jones 2004 and Petran 2012 found no overall association. 311 complaints are a noisy, self-selected signal of illness (Harrison 2014), which dilutes any effect.
prediction.support_if: The primary IRR has a 95% lower bound above 1.00 AND the ratio of the food-poisoning IRR to the Noise - Commercial IRR has a 95% lower bound above 1.00 (independence assumed for the ratio's variance, which is conservative when the two estimates covary positively).
prediction.refute_if: The primary IRR has a 95% upper bound below 1.10 (the low end of the band is excluded).
prediction.rule11: The placebo is the Noise - Commercial model. If its IRR has a 95% lower bound above 1.00 (it meets the first half of support_if), or D_placebo = z_placebo^2 - z_pred^2 < 4, where z_placebo = (b_fp - b_noise)/sqrt(se_fp^2 + se_noise^2) and z_pred = (b_fp - log 1.33)/se_fp, the verdict is unsettled unless refute_if is met.
prediction.power: Computed before the join from marginal counts (data/derived/restaurants/power_complaints.json): about 417.5 complaints at not-A and 562.6 at A-range restaurants expected; se(log IRR) 0.079 to 0.102 for dispersion 1.5 to 2.5; if the midpoint is true, z = 2.77 to 3.57 and D against no effect = 7.66 to 12.76 (>= 4, so the test discriminates the midpoint from no effect); at IRR 1.10 it does not (z about 1).

plan: Script analyses/restaurants/complaints_test.py at commit 0c147b3 (no resampling, no seed). Cohort: first Cycle Inspection / Initial Inspection with a score per CAMIS, 2023-01-01 to 2025-06-30, citywide live 43nn-pn8j, restricted to CAMIS whose 10-digit BBL holds exactly one CAMIS in the live data from 2022 on. Exposure: score >= 14 against 0-13. Outcome: count of erm2-nwe9 complaints, type Food Poisoning, location type Restaurant/Bar/Deli/Bakery, at the BBL, created on days 1-365 after the inspection. Model: Poisson GLM, HC1 robust SE, covariates borough, cuisine group (top 20), chain (dba with >= 10 CAMIS), inspection quarter. Placebo: same model with Noise - Commercial complaints at the BBL. Secondary, deciding nothing: C-range (>= 28) against A; per 10 points; NTA fixed effects; Manhattan only; complaints in the 365 days before the inspection.
alternatives: Volume: busy restaurants have more diners, so more complaints, and more chances for violations; the noise placebo and cuisine and chain controls address part of this.
Reporting propensity: neighbourhoods and clienteles that complain more to 311 also draw stricter inspections or are in areas inspected differently.
Persistent quality: a restaurant's hygiene is stable, so the association reflects the restaurant, not the inspection; the pre-window secondary shows this and does not make the result causal.
Survivorship: the live data keep only restaurants open now; restaurants that closed after a bad score and many complaints are missing, biasing the IRR towards 1.
Linkage: single-CAMIS BBLs are smaller buildings and differ from food halls and towers.
